cause: The annotator reads a sentence about a part, sub-part or quality as if the main part were missing. This covers a missing sub-part or appendage (keel, sheath, crest, pseudostalk, apical peg, lateral veins), 'not forming X', and a denied quality ('annulus not separating', 'annual constrictions absent').
remedy: Absence rule: the absent part is the noun after 'without/sans/lacking' or before 'absent'. The subject is the bearer, never the absent thing. If the absent noun or the denied quality does not ground, hold the row back. Never fall back to '<subject> absent'. Phrases like 'not forming X' and 'X not separating/falling' never produce PATO:0000462.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose bearer word is not the noun next to the negation cue in source_text (e.g. 'without keels' giving glume absent), or a negation cue followed by a verb ('not forming', 'not separating').
example: 'glumes without keels' gives glume absent. It should be keel-shaped, negated, on the glume, or keel PO:0025327 absent in the glume.

cause: The quality is put on the wrong part: the head organ of the sentence is used instead of the nearest part actually named (base, apex, lobe, segment, glomerule, petiole, flower stalk), or a position adjective is turned into a sub-part.
remedy: Prompt: 'The part is the nearest noun the quality is said of: in "base rounded", "apex of the lobe", "lateral lobes erect", "stigma lobes suborbicular", "ultimate segments 0.5 mm wide", the part is base/apex/lobe/segment of the named organ. In "apical bracts", "apical" is a position, not the bract apex.' Annotator: when source_text starts with 'base/apex/lobes/segments' and the bearer is the whole organ, re-ground to the sub-part class (leaf base, leaf apex, PO_0025517, corolla lobe FLOPO_0986006, stigma lobe FLOPO_0986009).
detectable: yes: the first noun of source_text (base, apex, lobe(s), segment(s), petiole, glomerule, stalk) does not match the transcribed part or its synonyms.
example: 'central lobe ..., apex long acuminate' was put on the leaf lamina. It belongs to the lobe apex.

cause: Missing-material statements ('not seen', 'not known', 'unknown', 'not observed', 'non vus') are recorded as the part being absent.
remedy: Add a hard drop rule in ncvc_annotate.py, applied before the absence check: if the span matches (not seen|not known|unknown|not observed|not available|not collected|inconnu\w*|non vu\w*), emit nothing. Transcription prompt: 'do not transcribe statements that material was not seen or not known'. Also remove 'sporophyte' → whole plant for moss floras.
detectable: yes: a regex on source_text of PATO_0000462 rows.
example: 'Flowers not known' gives flower absent, but the flowers of a fruiting specimen must have existed.

cause: A word that limits the statement (a position member such as dorsal, lateral or mid, a place such as along nerves, beneath, at base or central star, or a section heading such as female flowers or leaves in the synflorescence) is dropped, so the statement is said of the whole part.
remedy: Prompt: 'Copy every position word (dorsal, lateral, terminal/mid, basal, upper), place phrase (along veins, beneath/en dessous, à la face dorsale, at base, centre/star/eye) and section heading (male/female flowers, leaves in the synflorescence) into the qualifiers. When a series names its members, each number goes with its member.' Annotator: map these qualifiers to the position, place or whole slots through flora_context_words.tsv.
detectable: partly: source_text contains a place word from flora_context_words.tsv (dorsal, lateral, beneath, along, at base, en dessous) but the row's position or place slot is empty.
example: 'dorsal sepal obtuse' was stored as 'sepal obtuse'.

cause: A value word is grounded to the wrong PATO sense: 2-D terms used on solids, colour modifiers taken as the colour, a colour put on the organ instead of its hairs, false friends in French, and attribute terms used instead of values.
remedy: Lexicon rows that depend on the bearer type and the language: rounded or (sub)orbicular on a crown, fruit or seed → spherical or dome-shaped; (sub)entire → entire PATO_0104359; rugueux → rough; carinate → keel-shaped PATO:0002522; glabrate → glabrescent FLOPO:0991052; glaucous is not a colour. In '<modifier> <colour>' the head colour is the value. In '<colour>-tomentose' the colour goes on the hairs. A bare inflorescence measure is length, not height.
detectable: partly: a 2-D shape class on a solid bearer (fruit, seed, crown), an attribute-only quality (shape, colour) when source_text has a value word, or 'rugueu' grounded to rugose.
example: 'pome suborbicular, 10 mm diam.' gives orbicular (a flat outline). It should be spherical.

cause: The absence of a feature, substance or cell inclusion on an organ (dots, cystoliths, crystals, latex, chlorophyll, ant galls) is recorded as the organ being absent.
remedy: Add a table of feature and substance words, each with its reading: dots/epunctate → not punctate PATO_0001512 on the lamina; latex/sap/resin/crystals/cystoliths/tannins → hold back; chlorophyll/achlorophyllous → whole plant holomycotrophic FLOPO:0991374; ant galls → plant gall PO:0025626 absent. The annotator never moves their absence to the host organ.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose source_text contains a word from the feature/substance table and whose bearer is not that feature.
example: 'dots absent' gives leaf lamina absent. It should be lamina not punctate.

cause: A privative word said of one axis or region ('leafless flowering stems', 'scape ebracteate', 'leafless below', 'non florifères', 'never borne on the infl') becomes a plant-wide absence of the general part.
remedy: Rule: if leafless/ebracteate/without <part>/non-flowering sits in a clause whose subject is an axis (stem, scape, peduncle, branch, rameau), emit '<part> absent, located in <axis>' (cauline leaf absent on the axis, or a sterile branch), or hold it back. Never emit a taxon-level PO absence. 'never/not borne on X' is the position of the subject and gives no absence.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose source clause names an axis or region word (stem, scape, peduncle, branch, below, above) besides the absent part.
example: 'scape ebracteate' gives bract absent, which clashes with the phyllaries.

cause: The cue lists of existing patterns lack variants: other languages, a privative word, 'wanting', comparison or 'similar to', 'many-flowered', per-side and at-region cues, and stage phrases.
remedy: Add the cue rows: 'wanting'/'none' to NEGATION_EVIDENCE; French 'dépassant' = exceeding, 'de chaque côté' = each_side, 'base à N X' = at_region; 'similar to X but smaller/larger' gives size towards X; 'many-flowered' as an indefinite count, which 'not' can negate; 'at same time as / with the flowers' gives flowering stage PO:0007616; privative words (acaulescent, muticous) count as their own negation cue.
detectable: yes: the rows are already flagged existing_pattern with a missing-cue reason. List the unmatched spans that contain these words.
example: 'involucre wanting' is not read as involucre PO:0009100 absent.

cause: The PO lexicon synonym 'vein' → vascular bundle sends every statement about veins (vein orders, marginal vein, lateral veins, 'non nervié', 'not carinately veined') to one generic class, so unrelated statements clash.
remedy: Remove 'vein' from PO_0005020 in config/po_lexicon.tsv. Map vein words by context: leaf → leaf lamina vein PO_0020138, secondary/intersecondary/tertiary → their own PO classes, otherwise hold back. Annotator: 'not <adverb>ly veined' and 'no clear/distinct X vein' give no absence. '<organ> non nervié' is veinless on that organ.
detectable: yes: any row on PO_0005020 grounded from 'vein'/'nerve', and any absence row with an order or manner word before 'vein'.
example: 'intersecondary veins absent' gives vascular bundle absent, which clashes with the tertiary veins.

cause: Qualifier words are misread or invented: hedges and frequency words on an absence ('almost leafless', 'frequently absent'), degree words on a negation ('not markedly'), 'mostly' meaning extent, and qualifiers borrowed from a neighbouring clause.
remedy: A qualifier must come from a word inside the statement's span. Gate: almost, nearly, sub-, ±, frequently, often or sometimes before 'absent/leafless' blocks PATO:0000462 (read it as reduced, or drop). 'not markedly/very/strongly X' gives weakly X or nothing, never not X. 'mostly <state>' followed by a 'free parts/rest' clause is extent, not frequency.
detectable: yes: a qualifier on a row whose word does not occur in source_text, or an absence row whose span contains a hedge or frequency word.
example: 'almost leafless' gives leaf absent.

cause: A part word is grounded to the wrong PO class through a homonym, family-specific usage or prefix match (Carex utricle/perigynium, stipel → stipule, bud → generic bud, cycad 'spines' → thorn, Aristolochia limb/syrinx).
remedy: Add a family-scoped part table, looked up before po_lexicon. Cyperaceae: utricle/perigynium → PO_0009044. Remove perigynium from the involucral bract synonyms. Map stipel(s)/stipelle(s) → PO_0020051 with exact-word matching. 'bud' between calyx and corolla → flower bud. Cycad petiole 'spines' → petiole spine, not thorn PO_0025172. Aristolochiaceae: limb/syrinx/annulus/utricle → perianth parts. 'infructescence' → PO:0006342.
detectable: yes: the source word differs from the grounded label (stipel→stipule, utricle→fruit, spine→thorn), or a taxon family is in the family table.
example: 'Stipels 1–2 mm long' was grounded to stipule.

cause: Ranges and compound values are parsed incompletely: bracketed extremes limited to a context, 'N, rarely M', 'A X B mm', compound shapes, 'A-B to C', the second word of a range, and OCR-garbled numbers.
remedy: Prompt: 'A–B(–C in X): one row A–B, one row ≤C with context X. N, rarely M: M is an extreme. A × B unit: length A, width B. Keep compound shapes (oblong-elliptic) whole. In "A-B to C" the range runs from the compound A-B to C. Every word of a range keeps its value. Drop numbers that contain letters.' Annotator: check that each number in source_text appears in the row.
detectable: yes: numbers in source_text that are missing from value_low/high, or an 'X' or '×' between numbers with only one value used, or a hyphenated shape where only the first part is grounded.
example: '2–7(–12 in female flowers) mm' became 2–12 mm in female flowers.

cause: Count and comparison patterns fail because the container, landmark or target word is not grounded (ordinal scales, pistillate scale, per cell, per-side teeth container, laminate bract, calyx teeth/tube, '-celled').
remedy: Add container rows: 'the second (scale)' → upper glume PO:0006004; pistillate scale → bract of pistillate flower; 'per cell' as a per_unit kind; in a calyx sentence, 'teeth' → calyx lobe and 'tube' → calyx tube. The container of a per-side count is the organ that bears the counted parts, never the counted class. '<part> laminate' gives lamina present in <part>. '-celled' gives a cell count unless the bearer is an ovary or fruit.
detectable: yes: pattern rows with an empty or self-referential container, or an ungrounded target.
example: 'teeth 9–16 per side' was given the tooth class as its container, not the terminal leaflet.

cause: The numeric bound cues do not cover variants: parentheses, 'to more than', 'can reach', postposed 'or shorter/or less', FNA editorial brackets, and the inch sign.
remedy: Normalize source_text before matching: strip ˂ ˃ and parentheses around 'to N', and turn "/″ after a number into 'in'. Add cues: 'to more than' (strict lower bound), 'can reach' (upper bound), 'N unit long or shorter' and 'or less' (inclusive upper bound) to pattern 02.
detectable: yes: a number with a unit in source_text that produces no value row.
example: '˂to 20 cm˃' gives no height ≤ 20 cm.

cause: Process qualities (down, discontinuous, decreased rate) are put directly on structures, which makes classes unsatisfiable.
remedy: Lexicon: interrupted → PATO_0040026; continuous → its structural class; downward pointing / dirigés vers le bas → retrorse PATO_0002237 or descending FLOPO_0991207. Update the union pairs that use PATO_0000690. 'slow growing' → process pattern FLOPO_0980423, or drop.
detectable: yes: the quality is a subclass of process quality in PATO, or it fails the ELK unsat check.
example: 'raceme interrupted' gives PATO_0000690, a quality of a process.

cause: 'Bladeless (basal) sheaths' and 'the lower bladeless' become a taxon-wide leaf lamina absent in sedges and grasses, which have blades on their other leaves.
remedy: Rule: 'bladeless' with 'sheath(s)' or 'lower/basal' in the clause gives scale leaf PO:0006003, or lamina absent with the position 'basal sheaths'. Map 'sheaths' → leaf sheath PO:0020104. Never give a plain leaf lamina absent.
detectable: yes: a lamina-absent row whose source_text contains 'bladeless' together with 'sheath', 'lower' or 'basal'.
example: 'Basal sheaths bladeless' gives leaf lamina absent for Carex.

cause: Narrower lexicon synonyms of stem (caudex, culm, scape, stalk, trunk) pass their absence to stem PO:0009047.
remedy: In config/po_lexicon.tsv, mark caudex/caudices (and scape, culm, stalk) as narrow synonyms of PO_0009047. The annotator must not ground an absence through a narrow synonym: drop the row, or keep it with a 'caudex' context.
detectable: yes: an absence row on PO_0009047 whose source word is a narrow synonym.
example: 'caudex absent' gives stem absent, though the flowering stems are described.

cause: The modifier that names a subclass of the absent part (cauline, basal rosette, involucral, fine) is dropped, so the general class is denied.
remedy: Absence rule: ground the whole noun phrase first ('cauline leaves' → PO:0000013, 'basal rosette' → rosette leaf PO:0000014, 'involucral bract' → PO_0009045). If the phrase does not ground, hold the absence back. Never strip the modifier to reach the general class. Study observations ('were absent' at one site) are not taxon traits.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose source noun phrase has an adjective before the grounded head word.
example: 'cauline leaves absent' gives leaf absent, though there is a basal rosette.

cause: Grass and bamboo leaf-sheath parts (auricles, oral setae, oral hairs) are grounded to stipule, which creates false clashes. Coordinated absences also produce a presence.
remedy: For Poaceae: auricles → PO_0020106; oral setae and oral hairs → trichome at the sheath orifice; culm sheath → PO_0020104. Never stipule. Annotator: in 'X and Y absent' the negation covers every conjunct, and one source span may not yield both present and absent for one class.
detectable: yes: a Poaceae row on stipule PO_0020041, or one source_text that yields both PATO_0000467 and PATO_0000462.
example: 'auricles and oral setae absent' gives both stipule present and stipule absent.

cause: Habit nouns (liana, climber) have no reviewed rule.
remedy: Add habit rows (rule 6): liana → whole plant PO:0000003 ligneous PATO:0002348 and climbing FLOPO:0991108; climber → whole plant climbing FLOPO:0991108. Sizes are separate records.
detectable: yes: whole-plant rows with a habit noun in source_text and no quality.
example: 'Liana, up to 15 m' gives no habit annotation.

cause: Other: an alternative whose second member is a count ('entire or with 2 to 3 teeth') is read as a count per position.
remedy: Allow a union over full statements: entire OR (tooth amount 2–3, container leaf margin PO:0020128), with the pattern 03 count inside the second operand.
detectable: yes: 'or with N' inside a margin statement.
example: 'margin entire or with 2 to 3 teeth'.
